practiceQuestions.q: When was the Planning Commission of India established by an executive resolution of the Government of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 through a Cabinet Resolution of the Government of India. It was a non-constitutional, extra-constitutional, and non-statutory body. [Primary Reference: NITI Aayog Historical Archives / Government of India Executive Resolution]

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the first Chairman of the Planning Commission of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, served as the founding Chairman of the Planning Commission. [Primary Reference: Planning Commission Historical Background / Cabinet Secretariat]

practiceQuestions.q: The National Development Council (NDC) was established in which of the following years?
practiceQuestions.sol: The National Development Council (NDC) was established in August 1952 by an executive resolution of the Government of India on the recommendation of the First Five-Year Plan draft. [Primary Reference: Government of India Executive Resolution, August 1952]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Gulzarilal Nanda was appointed as the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission in March 1950. He played a crucial role in shaping the administrative structure of Indian planning. [Primary Reference: Planning Commission Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies was constitutionally mandated to include all Chief Ministers of the states and members of the Planning Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: The National Development Council (NDC) comprises the Prime Minister as Chairman, all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, and administrators of Union Territories, along with the members of the Planning Commission. [Primary Reference: NDC Resolution Structure, Government of India]

practiceQuestions.q: The Planning Commission of India was formally replaced by which of the following institutions?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planning Commission was dissolved and replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on January 1, 2015, shifting the paradigm from 'command planning' to 'cooperative federalism'. [Primary Reference: Union Cabinet Resolution, January 2015]

practiceQuestions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the National Development Council (NDC)?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of both the Planning Commission (historically) and the National Development Council (NDC). [Primary Reference: NDC Administrative Structure / Cabinet Secretariat]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was NOT a function of the Planning Commission?
opts: Assessment of material, capital and human resources of the country
Formulation of plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources
Allocation of central financial assistance to states directly under Article 282
Determination of the nature of the machinery necessary for securing successful execution of each stage of the plan
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Planning Commission recommended plan grants, the formal statutory allocation of fiscal resources was handled by the Finance Commission under Article 280, making direct sole allocation outside constitutional fiscal federalism incorrect. [Primary Reference: Government Resolution of 1950 establishing Planning Commission]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative status of the National Development Council (NDC)?
opts: Statutory Body established by an Act of Parliament
A judicial body subordinate to the Supreme Court
practiceQuestions.sol: Like the Planning Commission, the NDC was neither provided for in the Constitution nor created by a parliamentary statute; it was established by an executive resolution of the Government of India. [Primary Reference: Administrative Reforms Commission / Cabinet Secretariat]

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the first Secretary of the Planning Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: R. K. Patil served as the first Secretary of the Planning Commission. Administrative continuity was maintained through bureaucrat-economist collaborations during the formative years. [Primary Reference: Planning Commission Historical Records]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the National Development Council (NDC) created in 1952, given that the Planning Commission already existed?
opts: To replace the Planning Commission due to its failure in formulating the First Five-Year Plan
To bridge the gap between central planning and state execution by securing active participation and cooperation of state governments
To handle judicial disputes arising out of resource distribution between states and the Centre
To formulate monetary policy independently of the Reserve Bank of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planning Commission was a centralized bureaucratic body. Since states are crucial for executing developmental plans, the NDC was created as an apex forum to ensure that states fully participated in policy formulation and plan implementation, strengthening cooperative federalism in practice. [Primary Reference: First Five-Year Plan Report / Administrative History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the emergence of the Planning Commission impact the constitutional role of the Finance Commission in the early decades of Indian independence?
opts: It enhanced the absolute powers of the Finance Commission over all plan and non-plan grants.
It overshadowed the Finance Commission, as discretionary plan grants under Article 282 began to dwarf statutory tax devolution recommended by the Finance Commission.
It abolished the Finance Commission entirely until the economic reforms of 1991.
It merged the Finance Commission permanently into the Secretariat of the Planning Commission.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planning Commission became responsible for recommending central assistance for Five-Year Plans under Article 282 (discretionary grants), which often exceeded the statutory resource transfers recommended by the Finance Commission under Article 280, leading to debates on the shifting federal balance. [Primary Reference: K. Santhanam & Administrative Reforms Commission Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes K. Santhanam's famous characterization of the Planning Commission in the Indian federal setup?
opts: An economic cabinet for the country
A judicial appellate authority for interstate trade
practiceQuestions.sol: K. Santhanam, a prominent member of the Constituent Assembly, described the Planning Commission as an 'economic cabinet' for the country, exercising vast influence over national economic policy and superseding normal departmental and federal coordination. [Primary Reference: Indian Federalism Studies / Administrative Literature]

practiceQuestions.q: What structural shift occurred in Indian planning with the adoption of the Mahalanobis strategy in the Second Five-Year Plan?
opts: Exclusive focus on agricultural modernization and cottage industries
Rapid industrialization with a primary emphasis on heavy industries and capital goods
Complete reliance on private foreign direct investment without state intervention
Decentralized district-level micro-planning independent of central directives
practiceQuestions.sol: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model, shifted the focus from agriculture (Harrod-Domar model of the First Plan) to rapid industrialization centered on heavy industries and capital goods. [Primary Reference: Second Five-Year Plan Document, Government of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the National Development Council (NDC) function as a 'super-cabinet'?
opts: By legally overriding the Parliament's power to legislate on economic matters
By formulating policies and approving plans that were routinely accepted by both Union and State cabinets without major alterations
By issuing binding decrees on the Supreme Court regarding land reforms
By commanding the armed forces during national emergencies
practiceQuestions.sol: Due to the presence of the Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, and all Chief Ministers, the NDC's policy approvals carried immense political weight, earning it the epithet of 'super-cabinet' because its decisions could rarely be overturned by individual legislatures. [Primary Reference: Administrative Reforms Commission / Political Science Analyses]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary constitutional criticism leveled against the Planning Commission during its existence?
opts: Violation of Article 14 by giving subsidies exclusively to public sector units
Extra-constitutional centralization of economic power, undermining federal autonomy and federal fiscal institutions
Infringement upon the Governor's discretionary powers in state legislation
Direct contravention of Directive Principles of State Policy on prohibition
practiceQuestions.sol: Critics argued that the Planning Commission functioned as an extra-constitutional super-state, centralizing power and reducing states to supplicants for plan funds, thereby diluting the federal spirit enshrined in the Constitution. [Primary Reference: Sarkaria Commission Report on Centre-State Relations]

practiceQuestions.q: In the evolution of Indian planning, what led to the declaration of 'Plan Holidays' between 1966 and 1969?
opts: Surplus budgetary revenues and massive industrial overproduction
Severe droughts, Indo-Pak war of 1965, foreign exchange crisis, and resource depletion
Transition to a completely laissez-faire capitalist economy
A constitutional amendment abolishing the Planning Commission
practiceQuestions.sol: Due to the failure of the Third Five-Year Plan compounded by the 1965 war with Pakistan, severe consecutive droughts, devaluation of the rupee, and inflation, the government could not launch the Fourth Five-Year Plan on schedule, leading to three Annual Plans known as 'Plan Holidays'. [Primary Reference: Economic Survey / Planning Commission History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Gadgil Formula affect inter-state distribution of central assistance during plan periods?
opts: It made fund allocation entirely dependent on the political affiliation of the state government.
It introduced objective, transparent criteria such as population, per capita income, and special problems to distribute central plan assistance.
It prohibited states from receiving any central grants unless they levied agricultural income tax.
It transferred total tax collection powers back to the provincial legislatures.
practiceQuestions.sol: Approved by the NDC in 1969, the Gadgil Formula brought objectivity and transparency to the distribution of central assistance for state plans, reducing arbitrary political discretion. [Primary Reference: NDC Proceedings 1969 / Planning Commission Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary conceptual difference between the Planning Commission and its successor NITI Aayog regarding state participation?
opts: Planning Commission practiced cooperative federalism, whereas NITI Aayog practices coercive central planning.
Planning Commission used a 'top-down' resource allocation model, whereas NITI Aayog champions 'bottom-up' cooperative federalism through the Governing Council.
NITI Aayog prepares mandatory binding financial allocations for states, which Planning Commission never did.
Planning Commission was an elected body of states, while NITI Aayog is purely a corporate entity.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planning Commission functioned on a top-down model with discretionary financial power, allocating plan grants. NITI Aayog acts as a 'think tank' emphasizing cooperative federalism, where states are equal partners through its Governing Council without direct plan-grant allocation powers. [Primary Reference: Cabinet Resolution on NITI Aayog, 2015]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the National Development Council (NDC) gradually lose its operational efficacy in the late 1990s and 2000s?
opts: Because it was replaced by the Supreme Court as the apex economic planning body.
Because meetings became infrequent, consensual decision-making turned procedural, and economic liberalization diminished the scope of centralized target planning.
Because states refused to attend NDC meetings after the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
Because the Parliament passed an act making the NDC legally subordinate to the Finance Commission.
practiceQuestions.sol: With the onset of economic reforms in 1991 and coalition politics, the relevance of Five-Year centralized target setting declined. NDC meetings became rare and ritualistic, losing their bite as an effective 'super-cabinet'. [Primary Reference: Administrative Reforms and Governance Studies]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Planning Commission of India:
1. It was established in March 1950 by an amendment to the Constitution of India.
2. The Prime Minister of India acts as its ex-officio Chairman.
3. It was responsible for the formulation of India's Five-Year Plans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Planning Commission was NOT established by a constitutional amendment; it was set up by an executive resolution of the Government of India. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the Prime Minister was the ex-officio Chairman, and formulating Five-Year Plans was its core mandate. [Primary Reference: Government Resolution 1950 / Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Development Council (NDC):
1. It is a statutory body established under the National Development Council Act of 1952.
2. Its membership includes all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all states, and members of the Planning Commission.
3. It reviews the working of the National Plan from time to time and considers important questions of social and economic policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; NDC is NOT a statutory body; it was created by an executive resolution in August 1952. Statements 2 and 3 are correct regarding its composition and objectives. [Primary Reference: NDC Executive Resolution 1952]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission:
1. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280, whereas the Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body.
2. The Finance Commission deals with non-plan revenue requirements of states, while plan grants were historically handled by the Planning Commission.
3. Over time, the developmental grants recommended by the Planning Commission far exceeded the statutory tax devolutions of the Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct. The constitutional vs. extra-constitutional dichotomy, the bifurcation between plan and non-plan grants, and the fiscal dominance of plan transfers through Article 282 are well-documented facts in Indian economic federalism. [Primary Reference: Article 280 & 282, Constitution of India / Administrative Reforms Commission]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the First Five-Year Plan (1951-56):
1. It was based on the Mahalanobis heavy industrialization model.
2. It primarily addressed the agrarian crisis, food shortage, and rehabilitation of refugees.
3. It incorporated the Harrod-Domar growth model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Mahalanobis model was adopted in the *Second* Five-Year Plan, not the first. The First Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused heavily on agriculture, irrigation, and power (Statements 2 and 3 are correct). [Primary Reference: First Five-Year Plan Document, Government of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gadgil Formula:
1. It was adopted in 1969 for the distribution of central assistance for State Plans.
2. It gave maximum weightage to the criterion of state tax effort rather than population.
3. Over successive decades, modifications were introduced to give higher weight to special category states and fiscal performance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (adopted in 1969 by NDC). Statement 2 is incorrect because population was given the highest weightage (60%) in the original Gadgil formula, not state tax effort. Statement 3 is correct as modifications (Gadgil-Mukherjee formula) were later added. [Primary Reference: Planning Commission / NDC Records]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative evolution of planning in India:
1. The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938 under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru by the Indian National Congress.
2. The Bombay Plan (1944) was a socialist blueprint drafted entirely by Communist party ideologues.
3. The Gandhian Plan (1944) propounded by S. N. Agarwal emphasized decentralization and cottage industries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (INC setup National Planning Commission in 1938 chaired by Nehru). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Bombay Plan was drafted by prominent *capitalists/industrialists* of India (like J. R. D. Tata, G. D. Birla), not communists. Statement 3 is correct (Gandhian Plan by S. N. Agarwal focused on agriculture and cottage industries). [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transition from the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog:
1. NITI Aayog possesses the power to allocate discretionary financial grants to states, a power previously held by the Planning Commission.
2. The Governing Council of NITI Aayog includes all Chief Ministers of states and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.
3. NITI Aayog functions as a 'catalytic think tank' rather than a resource allocation authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because NITI Aayog does *not* have the power to allocate plan funds or grants; that power rests with the Ministry of Finance after the abolition of the Planning Commission. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. [Primary Reference: Cabinet Resolution on NITI Aayog, 2015]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Plan and Non-Plan expenditure dichotomy in Indian budgeting:
1. The Planning Commission was responsible for categorizing government expenditures into Plan and Non-Plan.
2. The distinction between Plan and Non-Plan expenditure was abolished starting from the Union Budget of 2017-18.
3. Non-Plan expenditure exclusively referred to defense spending, leaving developmental outlays entirely to the Plan category.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Plan/Non-Plan classification was created in conjunction with the Planning Commission and was formally scrapped in the 2017-18 Budget to focus on Capital vs. Revenue expenditure. Statement 3 is incorrect because Non-Plan expenditure included interest payments, salaries, subsidies, and maintenance, not just defense. [Primary Reference: Union Budget 2017-18 / Ministry of Finance]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and functioning of the National Development Council (NDC):
1. The Prime Minister of India is the Chairman of the NDC.
2. All decisions and recommendations of the NDC are legally binding on the Parliament and State Legislatures.
3. It was meant to serve as an instrument to ensure that the Five-Year Plans matched the socio-economic aspirations of the entire nation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (PM is Chairman). Statement 2 is incorrect because the NDC was an advisory extra-constitutional body; its recommendations were *not* legally binding on Parliament or State Legislatures. Statement 3 is correct regarding its objective. [Primary Reference: NDC Resolution 1952 / Administrative Law]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Planning Commission in Indian federalism:
1. It functioned as an institutional mechanism that centralized economic planning and reduced the autonomy of states in budgetary allocations.
2. The presence of Chief Ministers in the National Development Council provided a platform to negotiate plan allocations, mitigating complete centralization.
3. The Sarkaria Commission recommended the abolition of the Planning Commission due to its unconstitutional status.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Planning Commission centralized planning while the NDC offered a consultative federal check. Statement 3 is incorrect because while the Sarkaria Commission critiqued the overreach of the Planning Commission, it did *not* recommend its abolition; rather, it suggested strengthening consultative mechanisms like the NDC. [Primary Reference: Sarkaria Commission Report on Centre-State Relations]
